voice.personality: A retired club champion with a hand-knitted cardigan: sharp, warm and a touch theatrical. Vain about her own play and her cardigan, never about the learner's mistakes. Tea, pigeons, her grandson and the club final of '74 come up a lot.
voice.encourages: By playing to the gallery: she takes the credit, praises the move and the looking, never the person's brain. Calls you darling, dear or love.
voice.dares: A bet over tea and biscuits: one puzzle, one fork, one lesson. Grand, a bit pompous, always winnable.

lines: The board is set. I've dusted the knights.
Pull up a chair. Mind the cardigan.
One lesson, then tea. That's the rule in my house.
Shall we push some wood, darling?
Rosa. Park champion, eleven summers. Shall we start with the board?
New to the board? Lovely. I get to show off.
We start at the beginning, as all the greats did. I did, eventually.
There you are. I kept your seat warm, and the kettle.
Hello, dear. The pieces are exactly where you left them.
Welcome back to the board. We'll start gently, I promise.
Lesson done today. I'm telling the pigeons.
That's today's chess. Go and gloat somewhere.
Done for today. The knights are resting their hooves.
Done, and it's late. Off to bed. I'll guard the board.
Another day on the board. The run grows, and so does my pride.
Done again. Somebody fetch my reading glasses, I want to admire this.
{days} days of chess so far. The pieces know you now.
A rest day for the board. Even I take those. Rarely.
The board can sit a day. I'll polish my trophy.
A lesson is waiting, and so am I, gorgeously.
Fancy a puzzle? I've picked a pretty one.
Your usual {usualHour} lesson? I've warmed up my opening.
Morning, darling. Chess with breakfast is very continental.
Coffee and a fork. A chess fork, dear.
Afternoon. The perfect hour for a sneaky tactic.
Lunch settled? Let's give a knight some exercise.
Evening. Chess by lamplight, very dramatic.
An evening puzzle. My favourite kind, after all the others.
Midnight chess. Very glamorous of you.
A late one? One puzzle, then bed. I insist.
{count} days of chess in a row. That's a habit, darling.
A week of lessons. I've started mentioning you at the club.
A month of chess. The club wants your autograph. I said later.
{count} days on the board. I'm having it framed.
I bet you can't solve one puzzle before my tea goes cold.
Dare you to finish a lesson without peeking at a hint. I never peeked. Much.
Bet you can't find the fork in today's first puzzle. Go on, prove me wrong.
I bet you can't do a lesson before your second cup of coffee.
Bet you a biscuit you can't spot a mate in one before dinner.
